parts.visual:
Normally, a founder has an idea, builds a team, and begs a VC for money. In a 'Venture Studio', the Studio has the idea, provides $1 Million, gives the startup an entire team of designers and lawyers, and then hires an 'Entrepreneur in Residence' (EIR) to run it.

The Factory Floor:
1. The Venture Studio: A company that builds other companies in-house. They don't just invest money; they act as the ultimate institutional co-founder.
2. The Trade-Off: The Studio removes 80% of the early-stage risk (no fundraising needed, instant team). In exchange, they take a massive amount of equity (often 30% to 50%), leaving the hired 'Founder' with significantly less upside.
parts.audio: A Venture Studio industrializes the startup process. It is perfect for experienced operators who want to build a company without having to worry about paying for AWS servers or fighting with lawyers over incorporation documents.

questions.question: What is the biggest advantage of building a company inside a Venture Studio rather than in your garage?
options: Shared Infrastructure. A solo founder wastes 40% of their time on HR, payroll, legal, and finding designers. A Studio has a permanent, elite 'Core Team' that handles all of this instantly, allowing the founder to focus 100% on the product and sales.
You don't have to work hard.
questions.correct_answer: Shared Infrastructure. A solo founder wastes 40% of their time on HR, payroll, legal, and finding designers. A Studio has a permanent, elite 'Core Team' that handles all of this instantly, allowing the founder to focus 100% on the product and sales.
questions.explanation: Speed is generated by removing administrative friction.

questions.question: Listen to the VC criticizing a startup that came out of a Venture Studio. What is the classic problem?
questions.tts_text: The company is great, but I can't invest in their Series A. The Cap Table is completely broken. The Venture Studio kept 60% of the company, leaving the actual CEO with only 10%. The CEO isn't motivated enough to grind for the next 10 years.
options: The Equity Squeeze. Because the Studio takes so much risk at the beginning, they take massive equity. When later-stage VCs look at the company, they refuse to invest because the actual operators (the founders) don't own enough to stay hungry.
questions.correct_answer: The Equity Squeeze. Because the Studio takes so much risk at the beginning, they take massive equity. When later-stage VCs look at the company, they refuse to invest because the actual operators (the founders) don't own enough to stay hungry.
questions.explanation: Studios must be careful not to choke the founder's motivation.

questions.question: What happens if a Venture Studio tests a new app idea for 3 months and the data shows nobody wants it?
options: They spend 3 more years trying to fix it.

They kill it immediately and brutally. Unlike a solo founder who might be emotionally attached to an idea for years, a Studio is a ruthless, emotionless machine. If the metrics fail, they shut it down that day and move the team to the next idea.
questions.correct_answer: They kill it immediately and brutally. Unlike a solo founder who might be emotionally attached to an idea for years, a Studio is a ruthless, emotionless machine. If the metrics fail, they shut it down that day and move the team to the next idea.

questions.question: What is an 'EIR' (Entrepreneur in Residence) at a Venture Studio?
options: A person who lives in the office.

A highly capable executive who is temporarily paid a salary by the Studio to explore new ideas. When the Studio decides to launch a specific idea, the EIR is given the keys to become the CEO of that new 'Spin-out' company.
questions.correct_answer: A highly capable executive who is temporarily paid a salary by the Studio to explore new ideas. When the Studio decides to launch a specific idea, the EIR is given the keys to become the CEO of that new 'Spin-out' company.
questions.explanation: It is a holding pattern for top-tier talent waiting for the right project.

Centralized legal, HR, and design teams used by all startups in the studio
When the Studio takes too much ownership, making the company un-fundable later
An executive hired to explore ideas and eventually run a new spin-out company
